source.title: RankAlign: Vision-Language Representation Alignment via Rank Transformation
source.authors: En-Zhe Zhao; M. Fiorucci; Lamberto Ballan

record.file_problem: Full paper and appendices are present; no evident truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-modal class correspondence using rank-transformed relational kernels and compares outcomes with value-based matching and other transformations. This is a different measurement from the original claim’s scale-and-capability trend.
record.gate_note: The study measures class-level image-to-text correspondence recovery, not growth in representation alignment as model scale or capability increases. It compares transformations and reports results across datasets, label corruption, encoders, and class counts. Matching accuracy values used to select subsets are not separately recorded as outcomes. The paper also reports runtime results, which do not measure the claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses hypothesized shared relational structure to develop a class-permutation recovery method and reports matching accuracy. It does not measure convergence with capability, representation interchangeability with little loss, or convergence under alternative similarity metrics. Its normalization ablations and incomplete recovery establish properties of the matching pipeline, not V6 or V7: recovery also depends on class distinguishability and optimization error, as the paper explicitly shows.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' interpretation: they present ordinal class-correspondence recovery as strong support for the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and acknowledge prototype quality and matching complexity as limitations. Their conclusions go beyond the demonstrated result: monotone invariance alone does not guarantee robustness to arbitrary domain shifts or corruption, and correspondence recovery does not establish convergence with model capability.
record.recipe_differences: No reproduction of a scale-and-capability measurement. The study introduces rank-based kernel transformation and evaluates class-level unpaired correspondence recovery, comparing it with value-based and other normalized matching methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Matching outcomes change with kernel transformation, visual backbone, dataset, visual-label corruption rate, number of classes, and solver. RankAlign’s performance also varies across backbones and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: On identical CIFAR-100 prototypes and solvers, changing the relational transformation changes permutation recovery substantially; at N=100, raw and z-score kernels score 0.00, row-wise ranks 0.06, and RankAlign 0.79.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ordinal preprocessing can improve class-level correspondence recovery from frozen vision and language representations.

fits_no_version.finding: Matching performance depends on prototype corruption and dataset: ImageNet-100 accuracy falls from 74.4% to 41.5% at 40% corruption, while CIFAR-100 falls from 78.7% to 68.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-level correspondence recovery depends on the quality of class prototypes.

fits_no_version.finding: RankAlign recovers class correspondences under medical domain shift, with accuracy ranging from 0.23 to 0.65 across visual encoders.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ordinal class matching can work under domain shift, with substantial encoder-dependent limitations.

record.peer_reviewed: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)
record.problems: The experiments measure class-permutation recovery rather than direct representation similarity or a scale/performance trend. The scalability subsets are selected with a p-dispersion strategy favoring well-aligned relational structures. No model-capability measure or controlled comparison of training data/objectives is reported. Some ablation results have no uncertainty values, and the CheXpert results vary substantially across backbones.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 matching-accuracy results for N=50 and N=70 were not extracted; the N=100 solver comparisons were retained. Table 1 runtime results were omitted because they do not measure correspondence alignment. Figure-only curve values beyond the text’s approximate N=100 description were not transcribed.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability trend in representation alignment.
No alignment trend as vision and language models improve on paired images and captions.
No comparison of networks trained from different initializations; experimental seeds repeat matching.

Class permutation recovery does not measure replacing representations with little loss, stitching, or transferring a representation-dependent computation. Unsupervised Procrustes matching failure in Table 6 does not establish that a fitted linear map cannot enable interchangeability.
No identification of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
No comparison of measured representation convergence under alternative similarity measures, settings, or evaluation inputs; reported dependence concerns correspondence-recovery performance.
No direct measurement of completeness or plateau of alignment and no controlled test of shared training data or objectives as its cause.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded outcomes are method-performance results and should be excluded as claim-effect rows. Table 6 adds classical alignment comparisons, but these remain matching-method evaluations, so they are not missing claim results. Successful permutation recovery provides evidence of usable class-level relational compatibility, without measuring its completeness. Scalability subset selection explicitly uses corresponding cross-modal kernel entries; therefore zero-anchor matching does not imply that the entire evaluation construction is correspondence-free. LAION pseudo-classes also use caption-derived assignments. The supplied Table 1 is flattened and does not securely establish the reader's column attribution; its 0.98 values are plausibly N=50, with 0.79/0.79/0.91 at N=70 and 0.66/0.69/0.79 at N=100. This should be checked against the rendered table before retaining those performance rows.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep, and no test of alignment across independently trained models as they become larger or more capable.
No paired image-caption representation test, and no comparison of alignment as vision and language models improve.
Random seeds are repetitions of matching experiments, not a comparison of representations trained from different initializations.
The method recovers a class permutation; it does not test linear maps, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired representational interchangeability.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified across models.

Tests kernel transformation choices, class-count and data-condition effects, including visual-side label corruption and a medical dataset. Does not test alternative standard representation-similarity measures or settings such as varying neighbour counts.

Reports incomplete correspondence recovery in some settings. Does not isolate shared training data or objectives as causes, compare those causes with a common model of reality, or establish a plateau.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-100 kernel-transformation ablation across N=30, 50, 70, and 100
reader_labels.reason: Matching accuracy changes substantially with the relational transformation: RankAlign is highest at every reported size, while raw and generic normalization results are low (t5_n30_none through t5_n100_rankalign).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Different datasets, visual backbones, and visual-label corruption settings
reader_labels.reason: Results vary by backbone and dataset; corruption also reduces accuracy, particularly on ImageNet-100 at higher corruption rates (corrupt_cifar_0 through corrupt_imagenet_40; laion_*; chex_*).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-100, N=100 with CLIP and Sentence-T, across FAQ, OT, and FHG solvers
reader_labels.reason: RankAlign outperforms the value-based comparator with each reported solver, though the comparator’s accuracy depends strongly on solver (tab1_n100_faq_blind through tab1_n100_fhg_rank).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Larger matching problems and CheXpert class matching
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is incomplete in multiple conditions: the paper reports approximately 30% − 60% at N=100 across representative backbones, and CheXpert RankAlign accuracy ranges from 0.23 to 0.65 (scale_n100_text; chex_*_rank).
